title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer during regional failover + rate-limit hysteresis
author: Maya Chen
description:
Background: a customer incident (SUP-987) exposed a pathological interaction between the SLO Enforcer's circuit-breaker and the global rate-limiter during regional failover. When traffic was shifted to a fallback region the enforcer saw short, high-error bursts and aggressively opened the circuit while the rate-limiter concurrently issued client-side 429s. This caused coordinated over-shedding and prolonged degradation in downstream routes.

This PR introduces a targeted hotfix to reduce over-shedding and add short-term hysteresis and smoothing so that the enforcer differentiates between transient spike vs sustained violations during failover. Changes are conservative and limited to the enforcer runtime and configuration so they can be safely backported to the current release branch if needed.

What I changed (summary):
- Add short-duration hysteresis window to the SLO enforcer's circuit-breaker logic: require a minimum sustained error-rate for 2s before fully tripping; add exponential smoothing to the rolling error-rate estimate.
- Add rate-limit-aware downgrade path: when upstream 429s are dominant, the enforcer will prefer gradual shedding and increase the backoff window rather than immediate full circuit open.
- Tighten fallback ordering to prefer capacity-tiered regions (dedicated > hosted) during automated routing transitions.
- Add additional metrics and logs: slo_enforcer.hysteresis_ms, slo_enforcer.smoothed_error_rate, slo_enforcer.rate_limit_backoff_count for post-incident analysis.
- Include unit and integration tests that simulate failover + rate-limit storm and assert no >5s sustained full-shed windows.
- Small config defaults change in deploy/k8s/slo-enforcer-config.yaml to safe conservative thresholds.

Why this is safe: the change only alters the enforcer's decision thresholds and smoothing; the default behavior remains unchanged for normal steady-state traffic and the hysteresis is short (2s) to avoid compromising SLO enforcement. Added metrics and tests improve observability and confidence.

Review notes and conversation (condensed):
- Asha Patel: "Observed the same incident in staging earlier; LGTM approach but please ensure we avoid introducing new flapping windows. Can the smoothing alpha be made configurable?"
- Maya Chen: "Made alpha configurable via ENV and added integration tests for two alpha values (0.2, 0.6). Also added a guard to prevent alpha >= 0.9 to avoid masking sustained failures."
- Diego Rivera: "Please validate that the backoff path doesn't add extra 429s to caller when the downstream is healthy. Unit tests look good; integration pending."
- Liam O'Connor: "Left one nit on variable naming and a small race fix in the rate-limit counter; suggested adding a small lock around update path."
- Maya Chen: "Addressed the naming/race comments in follow-up commit; re-ran unit+integ."
